traits.notes: The seedling exhibits a whorled leaf arrangement with simple, elliptic leaves that are shiny and glabrous. Leaves are arranged in clusters at nodes, with no visible petiole elongation. Stem is short and woody, with no trichomes or latex. Some minor surface damage (small holes or spots) is visible on a few leaves, but cause is not identifiable. All images show the same individual from various angles, confirming consistent morphology. No habitat details are clearly visible beyond leaf litter substrate.

data.raw_response:
=== Morphological Assessment Form ===
A. Leaf Arrangement & Architecture
    1. Leaf relative position (alternate / opposite / whorled): whorled (multiple leaves are clearly attached at the same node, visible in close-up images; at least 3 leaves per node)
    2. Leaf spacing (clustered / distal): clustered (leaves are grouped closely at nodes along the stem, with no long internodes visible)
B. Leaf Complexity
    3. Leaf complexity (simple / compound): simple (each leaf is a single, undivided blade)
    4. Compound leaf type, ONLY if leaf complexity is compound (odd-pinnate / even-pinnate): N/A
    5. Number of leaflets (integer estimate 2, 4, 8, …): N/A
    6. Leaflet arrangement (opposite / alternate / subopposite): N/A
C. Leaf Morphology
    7. Leaf margin (entire / toothed) AND if toothed (dentate, serrate, etc.)): entire (smooth margin with no visible teeth or serrations)
    8. Leaf shape (elliptic, obovate, lanceolate, etc.): elliptic (broad in the middle, tapering to both ends, with a rounded base and acute apex)
    9. Leaf apex (acute, obtuse, acuminate): acute (tapering to a sharp point)
    10. Leaf base (rounded, cordate, cuneate): rounded (blunt and gently curved at the base)
    11. Venation type (pinnate / palmate / parallel): pinnate (main vein running from base to apex, with lateral veins branching off and arching toward the margin)
    12. Secondary veins (visibility, spacing, number): visible, spaced moderately, 3–5 pairs per leaf (clearly visible as arching veins from midrib to margin)
    13. Leaf surface features (glabrous, shiny, dull, rugose): shiny, glabrous (surface is smooth and glossy, reflecting light)
    14. Leaf surface trichomes (present / absent): absent (no visible hairs or fuzz on leaf surface)
    15. Petiole length (short / long): short (petiole is short and stout, barely visible in some images)
    16. Petiole features (winged / grooved / terete): terete (circular in cross-section, not flattened or winged)
D. Stem & Shoot Traits
    17. Stem type, may not be visible (woody / herbaceous): woody (stem appears firm and slightly woody, with a brownish, textured surface)
    18. Stem trichomes (present / absent): absent (no visible hairs on stem surface)
    19. Stem color: green to brownish (young stem is green, older portions appear brownish)
    20. Stem texture (smooth / ridged / lenticellate): smooth (surface appears smooth without ridges or lenticels; slight texture may be due to growth rings or fine surface)
E. Other Visible Seedling Traits
    21. Stipules, sometimes visible only in close-up images (present / absent): absent (no stipules visible at leaf bases)
    22. Latex, rarely visible but extremely diagnostic when present (present / not observed): not observed (no exudate visible when stem is broken or damaged)
    23. Pulvinus, for Fabaceae family only (present / absent): absent (no swollen joints at leaf bases or petiole bases)
    24. Tendrils (present / absent): absent (no tendrils observed)
F. Notes: The seedling exhibits a whorled leaf arrangement with simple, elliptic leaves that are shiny and glabrous. Leaves are arranged in clusters at nodes, with no visible petiole elongation. Stem is short and woody, with no trichomes or latex. Some minor surface damage (small holes or spots) is visible on a few leaves, but cause is not identifiable. All images show the same individual from various angles, confirming consistent morphology. No habitat details are clearly visible beyond leaf litter substrate.
